From: Suzanne Blake <suzanne.blake@healtiva.com>

Cc: LegalOps <legalops@healtiva.com>

Subject: DPA questions: certification for non-learning + subprocessor gating

Hi Karthik / Marissa,

Thanks for the demo last week. Legal has one set of stickier asks before procurement can sign the SOW: they want a clear, operational commitment that Healtiva data will not be used to improve or fine-tune shared models (no-adaptive-training), plus evidence we can provide to auditors that subprocessors are gated (and that any transfers out of EU are documented).

Specifically they asked for:
- A short attestation we can include in our DPA that Redwood will not use Healtiva prompts/responses for model training outside of our dedicated tenant (no-learning).
- Details on how Redwood gates subprocessors (approval workflow, third-party attestations, and a timeline for onboarding/changes).
- Export path for derived artifacts: if Healtiva requests copies of interaction logs + derived embeddings, what is the process and expected format? They want this to be feasible via SFTP or signed transfer, with proof of deletion after transfer.

I've attached Legal's question bundle. Can you review and confirm what evidence/ops language we can provide? Procurement is on a tight timeline so any clear templates or attestations would help.

Best,
Suzanne
Head of Procurement, Healtiva

Attachments: healtiva_dpa_questions_20280612.pdf

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, David Kim <david@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 12 Jun 2028 11:03:00 +0000
Subject: Fwd: DPA questions: certification for non-learning + subprocessor gating

Marissa / David — forwarding Healtiva's legal bundle. Key asks: no-learning attestation, subprocessor gating evidence, and an export+deletion workflow (SFTP preferred).

My thoughts / quick notes:
- We can provide a one-paragraph attestation on no-adaptive-training for tenant-bounded data; reference the control that tenant data is logically isolated and cannot be ingested into shared model training pipelines. We should avoid legalese guarantees about future model releases but provide operational evidence (audit logs + KV cache isolation).
- For subprocessors: supply our current inventory + the gating workflow (security review, contract clauses, periodic attestations). We have an internal doc (I can attach) but legal will want a sign-off cadence and change-notice SLA (30 days).
- Export path: Ops can produce a signed SFTP bundle (CSV + gzipped transcripts + embedding dump) and a deletion certificate. We should clarify timelines (48-72h prep, delivery window, 30-day retention after transfer unless otherwise requested).

Questions for David: can we produce the attestation as a DocuSign-ready statement? Also need confirmation that the SFTP export includes SHA256 manifests and that deletion certs are generated from the same logs.

If you both agree I'll draft language and a short attestation doc for Suzanne.

—Karthik

From: David Kim <david@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 12 Jun 2028 13:27:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Fwd: DPA questions: certification for non-learning + subprocessor gating

Karthik / Marissa — quick ops confirmation:
- Attestation: Ops can produce a DocuSign-ready attestation. Suggested text below (we should run through Legal for sign-off):
  "Redwood Inference attests that data submitted by Healtiva to the Healtiva tenant will not be used to update, retrain, or otherwise improve Redwood's shared public models. Data will be processed only within the customer-dedicated environment unless expressly accepted into a separate training program under a signed agreement."

- Subprocessor gating: we maintain a live inventory and require a security review and contract addendum before onboarding. We can provide a snapshot export (signed) plus a statement of the change-notice SLA (we publish a 30-day notification for any new subprocessor that would process EU data). We can add a clause that critical subprocessors will provide SOC2-type attestations on request.

- Export & deletion: We can generate an SFTP bundle with per-file SHA256 manifests, a signed delivery receipt, and a deletion certificate referencing the object IDs. Timeline: 72 hours to prepare exports after formal request; deletion cert within 7 days after confirmed ingestion on customer side. We will also include an operational runbook describing the steps.

I recommend we include one operational exhibit in the DPA describing the export payload schema and the deletion certificate format. I can draft the runbook and the sample manifest.

-David

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
To: Suzanne Blake <suzanne.blake@healtiva.com>, LegalOps <legalops@healtiva.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, David Kim <david@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 14 Jun 2028 16:23:00 +0000
Subject: Re: DPA questions: certification for non-learning + subprocessor gating

Suzanne / Healtiva Legal — thanks for the clear list. We've reviewed with Ops and Legal on our side and can provide the following package to support your DPA: 

1) Scoped attestation (DocuSign-ready) confirming no-adaptive-training for tenant data. Wording is operational (see draft below) and excludes platform-level research programs unless a separate agreement is signed.

2) Subprocessor evidence bundle: current inventory snapshot (CSV), description of the gating process (security review + contract addendum), and our change-notice SLA of 30 days for subprocessors that would process EU customer data. Critical subprocessors will be accompanied by their most recent third-party assurance reports where available.

3) Export & deletion runbook: an ops exhibit describing the SFTP export payload (transcripts csv, embeddings ndjson, SHA256 manifest), expected timelines (72h prep), delivery confirmation, and a deletion certificate issued by Redwood within 7 days of confirmed receipt.

4) Implementation note: for extra assurance we can tag Healtiva tenant interactions with an "opt-out-for-improvement" flag system-wide so logs and prefixes are excluded from any experimental model pipelines. This is already implementable at routing time and we will document it in the exhibit.

Next steps: I will attach the draft attestation and the subprocessor snapshot by end of day tomorrow and include a sample deletion certificate and SFTP manifest for your review. If that meets Legal's needs we can move to a DocuSign attestation and close procurement.

Would you like the attestation sent directly to LegalOps or to Procurement contact first?

Thanks — looking forward to closing this quickly.

Regards,
Karthik Iyer
Head of Sales, Redwood Inference
